s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive low back and lower extremity pain with nighttime worsening in a pediatric patient
salient_findings: Progressively worsening low back pain and bilateral lower extremity pain
Intradural and extramedullary lesion at the L3 level on MRI
key_facts: 10-year-old boy
Two months of progressively worsening low back pain
Bilateral lower extremity pain
Pain worse at night and on waking
Difficulty bending at the waist
No sensory or motor deficits
No bladder or bowel dysfunction
Hyperdense lesion at the L3 level on lumbar spine CT
Intradural and extramedullary lesion on MRI
Lesion displaced the cauda equina ventrally
Faintly hyperintense on T1-weighted images
Hypointense on T2-weighted images
Uniform contrast enhancement without a dural tail sign
No additional lesions on MRI of the cervical, thoracic, and intracranial compartments

differentials: Spinal metastasis from a rare tumor
Spinal subarachnoid hemorrhage from a spinal arteriovenous malformation
Spinal cord infarction due to fibrocartilaginous embolism
per_call: Spinal metastasis from a rare tumor
Spinal subarachnoid hemorrhage from a spinal arteriovenous malformation
Spinal cord infarction due to fibrocartilaginous embolism

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Intradural and extramedullary lesion with uniform contrast enhancement, consistent with meningioma characteristics

shortlist.label: Clear cell meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Specific subtype of meningioma, considered due to the patient's age and lesion appearance

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the intradural and extramedullary location, although less likely than meningioma

shortlist.label: Myxopapillary ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present as an intradural and extramedullary lesion, worth considering in the differential

shortlist.label: Spinal meningeal melanocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Uncommon tumor that could explain the patient's symptoms and imaging findings, although less common than meningioma

raw.rationale: The lesion's location in the lumbar spine, specifically at the L3 level and being intradural and extramedullary, along with its imaging characteristics such as being faintly hyperintense on T1-weighted images and hypointense on T2-weighted images, and the absence of a dural tail sign, are more consistent with a myxopapillary ependymoma, especially given the age of the patient and the specific symptoms presented.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Less common in pediatric population and the absence of a dural tail sign makes it less likely

rejected.label: Clear cell meningioma
rejected.why: Similar reasons as for meningioma, with the added consideration that clear cell meningiomas are rare and the described imaging characteristics are not as typical for this subtype

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Typically shows a different pattern of enhancement and often has a more eccentric location within the spinal canal

rejected.label: Spinal meningeal melanocytoma
rejected.why: These are rare pigmented tumors that would likely have different imaging characteristics, particularly on T1-weighted images due to the melanin content
